text: The book examines fₙ(x) = xⁿ on [0, 1], whose pointwise limit is 0 on [0,1) and 1 at x = 1. What does this example demonstrate?
choices: That uniform convergence can fail to preserve continuity.
That pointwise convergence of continuous functions can produce a discontinuous limit, so the convergence here is not uniform.
That every pointwise-convergent sequence of continuous functions has a continuous limit.
That the limit function is continuous because each fₙ is continuous.
explanation: The book uses fₙ(x) = xⁿ to show a pointwise limit of continuous functions may be discontinuous (a jump at x = 1); since a uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous, this convergence cannot be uniform, and indeed sup|fₙ − f| = 1 for every n. Option 0 misattributes the failure to uniform convergence, which actually preserves continuity, while options 2 and 3 assert the very conclusion the counterexample refutes.
